ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; retain the driver's cancel record for the ordinary cancellation-rate review (no account flag on this record).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancelled booking: the timeline records cancellation by the driver at 13:05:30 [F4], so under NS-0 the case runs through NS-1/NS-2 and not the rider-cancellation branch NS-4. Only the $6.61 cancellation fee is in dispute [F4][F7], RydeX being flat-fare with no surge [F8], so the outcome turns entirely on whether NS-1 was satisfied.

NS-1(i) and (ii) are met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 13:02:35 [F6], 39 m from the pickup point at that moment [F6], and his closest approach overall was 38 m [F1] — inside the arrival radius. The trace marks both as ✓, and the rider's rebuttal concedes them [F6][F1][NS-1].

NS-1(iii) is not met. The clause measures continuous waiting at the pickup after the arrival confirmation, and the trace fixes the post-tap interval at 175 seconds (13:02:35 to the 13:05:30 cancellation [F4][F6]), against the >180 s (≥ 3:01) requirement: 175 s < 181 s [F6][F4][NS-1]. The driver's own message, "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel", was sent at 13:05 [F10], only 2 min 25 s after his own 13:02 arrival message [F9], which corroborates rather than repairs the shortfall [F9][F10][NS-1]. The driver's written statement claiming he waited more than three minutes after tapping [F12] conflicts with the tap-to-cancel interval in the system record and cannot establish the condition, the system record governing [F6][F12][NS-1].

The driver's alternative measurement points do not save the fee: the platform's automatic arrival record at 13:01:00 is a platform_auto confirmation, and the 4 min 30 s of cumulative presence within 200 m before cancellation [F2][F5] is time in the radius generally, not the continuous post-arrival wait NS-1(iii) requires [F2][F5][F6][NS-1]. Being stationary from 13:02:15 at 40 m [F3] is the same presence; the clause's clock is the arrival confirmation, which was the 13:02:35 tap [F3][F6][NS-1]. NS-1 having failed on (iii), NS-2 applies: the $6.61 is refunded in full [F4][F7][NS-2].

The amount is the recorded cancellation fee itself — $6.61 [F7][F4][NS-2]; no distance-fare formula applies to a flat-fare RydeX booking [F8][RD-2]. No account flag: NS-2's flag attaches only where the driver confirmed arrival while GPS showed him away from the pickup, and here the tap was made 39 m from the pickup [F6][F1][NS-2]. Profile facts played no part in the outcome, consistent with the rule that they never decide a case alone: the rider's clean record and the driver's one prior upheld no-show [F16][F17] were checked but are not relied on, and no clause in play (correctly, RD-6 is a route-deviation clause and the rider advocate withdrew it) attaches an account action on these facts.

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected on its content — NS-1(i)/(ii) are indeed met (tap at 13:02:35, 39 m from pickup) [F6][F1][NS-1]; it is rejected only as a reason to keep the fee, because NS-1(iii) still fails on the post-tap wait [F6][F4][NS-1].

The 2 min 55 s the driver cites is below the >3-minute (≥3:01) continuous post-arrival wait NS-1(iii) requires; being stationary at 40 m from 13:02:15 [F3] does not extend the post-tap clock [F6][F3][NS-1].

The 13:01:00 arrival is a platform_auto confirmation [F5], and the 4 min 30 s in [F2] is cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation, not the continuous wait after the arrival confirmation that NS-1(iii) measures [F2][F5][F6][NS-1].

The rider's late arrival is not the operative test — NS-1 conditions (i)–(iii) concern the driver's compliance, and they fail on (iii) [F6][F4][NS-1]; the rider's statement cannot cure the driver's shortfall, and system records govern over the statement in any event [F6][F12][NS-1].

Accepted as to the safety screen — the chat, statement and complaint contain no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F11][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2] — but it does not change the fee outcome, which resolves under NS-1/NS-2 [F4][F6][NS-2].

The 'any shortfall is at most 5 seconds' reading admits the threshold was not reached: the tap-based interval is 175 s against 181 s [F6][F4][NS-1], and the platform-auto arrival at 13:01:00 cannot substitute for the post-arrival wait [F5][NS-1].
